questions.text: The investor’s ultimate record of ownership in mutual funds held in demat form is maintained by:
questions.explanation: In demat mode, the Depository Participant (DP) maintains the record of ownership under the investor’s demat account.

questions.text: A positive cash-flow surplus can be used for:
questions.explanation: Surplus cash can build assets or reduce liabilities.

questions.text: “Investment-grade” debt generally refers to:
options: Debt rated in the lower categories indicating high default risk
Debt with credit ratings in higher categories indicating relatively lower default risk
Debt that has no rating but is issued by start-ups
Any government bond irrespective of rating
questions.explanation: Investment-grade ratings indicate relatively lower default risk compared to non–investment grade or ‘junk’ ratings.

questions.text: From a small retail investor’s perspective, which channel is usually the MOST suitable for diversification with low ticket size?
questions.explanation: Mutual funds allow small investors to achieve diversification with low ticket sizes and professional management.

questions.text: If a client insists on a speculative strategy beyond their risk profile, the adviser should:
options: Accept immediately to earn more fees
Explain risks, document the discussion, and, if still unsuitable, decline or limit the engagement
questions.explanation: Ethically, the adviser must educate, document, and avoid participating in clearly unsuitable strategies.

questions.text: A put option gives the holder:
options: The right but not obligation to sell the underlying asset at a fixed price
The obligation to buy the underlying asset
The right to receive a dividend
questions.explanation: A put option gives the buyer the right to sell the underlying asset at a specified price before or on expiry.

questions.text: If an investor receives ₹10,000 every year for 5 years, the present value at 8% p.a. is (approx.):
Which of these is a constraint that may affect personal financial planning?
questions.explanation: Income, responsibilities and the regulatory framework all act as constraints that the plan must consider.

questions.text: A positive Jensen’s Alpha indicates:
options: Portfolio outperformed relative to its systematic risk
questions.explanation: A positive alpha means the portfolio delivered higher return than expected for its risk level, indicating superior management.

questions.text: Redemption proceeds of NRI investments made on a non-repatriable basis are credited to:
questions.explanation: Non-repatriable proceeds are credited to the NRO account of the NRI investor.

questions.text: Which entity manages the portfolio and day-to-day operations of a mutual fund scheme?
questions.explanation: The Asset Management Company (AMC) manages the scheme, including investments, marketing and investor servicing.

questions.text: An individual buying a flat purely as an investment (not for self-use) is MOST likely investing in which asset class?
questions.explanation: A flat purchased for investment purposes is real estate, a tangible asset class.

questions.text: The formula for the expected return of a portfolio is:
options: Weighted average of expected returns of individual securities
Sum of variances of individual securities
questions.explanation: Expected portfolio return is the weighted average of expected returns of its constituent securities.

questions.text: Holders of equity shares are known as:
questions.explanation: Equity shareholders are owners and have residual claims on assets and profits.

questions.text: Which entity holds the securities and assets of an AIF in custody?
questions.explanation: A registered custodian is mandatory for all Category III AIFs and for Category I and II AIFs with corpus ≥ ₹500 crore.

questions.text: Self-Regulatory Organizations (SROs) in securities markets must:
options: Always act in the best interest of investors and abide by SEBI directions
Have no role in member supervision
questions.explanation: SROs must follow SEBI’s directions, supervise members, and act in the interest of investors.

questions.text: The coefficient of determination (R²) measures:
options: The degree of correlation between portfolio and market returns
The total variance of portfolio returns
questions.explanation: R² measures how much of a portfolio’s movements can be explained by market movements, indicating diversification benefits.

questions.text: The main contribution of Modern Portfolio Theory is that it:
options: Quantified diversification using covariance or correlation between assets
questions.explanation: MPT quantified diversification benefits using statistical tools like covariance and correlation to manage risk.

questions.text: A bond trades at a premium to face value when:
options: Coupon rate is equal to the current market yield
Coupon rate is higher than the current market yield
Coupon rate is lower than the current market yield
questions.explanation: If the bond’s coupon exceeds the market yield, investors are willing to pay more than face value, so the bond trades at a premium.

questions.text: A 25-year-old with no dependants and stable income is generally more suitable for which allocation?
options: Very high proportion of assets in cash only
Higher allocation to growth assets such as equity
questions.explanation: With long time horizon and low dependants, growth assets like equity can form a higher proportion of the portfolio.

questions.text: A cash-flow deficit indicates that:
questions.explanation: Deficit means spending more than earnings; corrective action needed.

questions.text: Which of the following measures a stock’s sensitivity to market movements?
questions.explanation: Beta measures the stock’s volatility relative to the overall market.

questions.text: Borrowers should ideally limit total EMI outgo to:
questions.explanation: Total EMIs beyond 40% strain cash flow and risk defaults.

questions.text: The main advantage of secured loans over unsecured loans is:
options: Lower interest rates due to collateral
questions.explanation: Collateral reduces lender’s risk, allowing lower interest rates.

questions.text: Which statement about bond prices and interest rates is TRUE?
options: Bond prices and interest rates move in the same direction
Bond prices are unaffected by interest rates
Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions
Bond prices always equal face value
questions.explanation: There is an inverse relationship: when market yields rise, bond prices fall and vice versa.

questions.text: The SEBI (Investment Advisers) Regulations were introduced in:
questions.explanation: The SEBI (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013 govern the registration and conduct of investment advisers in India.

questions.text: A key distinguishing feature of a mutual fund compared to PMS is that:
options: Mutual funds are unregulated, while PMS is regulated
Mutual funds pool money from many investors into a common portfolio, while PMS maintains segregated portfolios for each client
Mutual funds are only for HNIs, while PMS is for small investors
Mutual funds can invest only in equity
questions.explanation: Mutual funds operate a common pool of assets, whereas PMS typically runs segregated portfolios in each client’s name.

questions.text: Which regulator handles insurance-related investor complaints?
questions.explanation: IRDAI regulates insurance entities and handles insurance-related grievances.

questions.text: Why should cash-flow statements be reviewed periodically?
options: Income and expenses remain constant always
To identify changes in income, expenses or new commitments early
questions.explanation: Regular review keeps the plan aligned with life changes and goals.

questions.text: Which of these statements about budgeting is TRUE in the context of financial planning?
options: Budgeting is only for low-income households
Budgeting tracks income and expenses to identify savings potential
Budgeting is not needed if one invests in mutual funds
Budgeting is done only once a year and not revisited
questions.explanation: Budgeting helps monitor cash flows and create surplus that can be directed towards goals.

questions.text: Portfolio Managers can invest a maximum of ___% of a client’s portfolio in their own associate or related companies.
questions.explanation: As per SEBI, the cap is 30% with prior written consent from the client.

questions.text: In a multi-cap fund, SEBI requires that at least 75% of assets are in equity with minimum allocation of:
options: 25% in large-cap, 25% in mid-cap, 25% in small-cap
questions.explanation: Multi-cap funds must invest at least 75% in equity-related instruments, with a minimum of 25% each in large, mid and small-cap stocks.

questions.text: Category I AIFs generally invest in:
questions.explanation: Category I AIFs include venture-capital, SME, social-venture and infrastructure funds that create positive economic impact.

questions.text: A high proportion of discretionary expenses may indicate:
questions.explanation: Too much discretionary spending can reduce savings and create deficits.

questions.text: Overnight funds invest in securities with a maturity of:
questions.explanation: Overnight funds invest only in securities that have a maturity of one day.

questions.text: Which of the following is a common equity derivative traded on Indian exchanges?
options: Index futures and options on Nifty 50 and Sensex
questions.explanation: Equity derivatives such as Nifty 50 and Sensex futures/options are widely traded on NSE and BSE.

questions.text: A family has monthly income ₹1,50,000, total expenses ₹1,35,000 including ₹30,000 discretionary. What is the discretionary expense ratio?
questions.explanation: 30,000 ÷ 1,50,000 = 20% actually? Wait check: 30/150 = 0.2 = 20%; adjust to 20% (index 1).

questions.text: Expected return of an individual security is calculated as:
options: Sum of potential returns divided by number of outcomes
Sum of possible returns weighted by their respective probabilities
Return on risk-free security plus risk premium
questions.explanation: Expected return is computed by summing potential returns multiplied by their probabilities.

questions.text: If the Sharpe Ratio of a portfolio is less than that of the market, it indicates:
options: Portfolio underperforms on a risk-adjusted basis
questions.explanation: A lower Sharpe Ratio than the market indicates inferior risk-adjusted performance.

questions.text: Which of the following principles ensures PMS fees are not charged twice for the same performance?
questions.explanation: Under the high-watermark principle, performance fees are charged only when portfolio value exceeds its previous peak.

questions.text: In mutual fund transactions, the term 'folio number' refers to:
options: Unique identification number for each investor account
questions.explanation: Each investor account with an AMC is assigned a unique folio number for identification and record-keeping.

questions.text: Dividend reinvestment option in mutual funds means:
options: Dividends are paid out to the investor’s bank account
Dividends are used to buy additional units in the same scheme
questions.explanation: Under the dividend reinvestment option, declared dividends are reinvested to purchase additional units in the same scheme.

questions.text: Investors can check mutual fund unclaimed dividends and redemptions through:
questions.explanation: AMFI hosts a centralized portal for checking and claiming unclaimed amounts across AMCs.

questions.text: Ethically communicating risk to clients requires:
options: Highlighting only high returns in presentations
Presenting both upside potential and downside risks clearly
questions.explanation: Balanced communication should clearly explain possible losses, volatility, and risk factors along with potential returns.

questions.text: Repatriable NRI investments must be made from:
questions.explanation: For repatriable investments, funds must come through NRE or FCNR accounts maintained with Indian banks.

questions.text: A decrease in net worth may be due to:
questions.explanation: Borrowing or fall in asset values can reduce net worth.

questions.text: Depository Participants (DPs) function as:
options: Agents of depositories who open and maintain demat accounts for investors
questions.explanation: DPs act as agents of depositories for investors, opening demat accounts and facilitating securities transfers.

questions.text: Discretionary Portfolio Managers:
options: Execute client trades only after client approval
Have full discretion to manage funds as per the agreed mandate
Can act as mutual fund distributors
questions.explanation: Discretionary Portfolio Managers manage and invest client funds independently as per the client’s mandate.

questions.text: If total assets = ₹60 lakh and total liabilities = ₹25 lakh, the individual’s net worth is:
questions.explanation: Net Worth = Assets − Liabilities = 35 lakh.

questions.text: A stock split means:
options: Company merges two shares into one
Company divides each share into smaller units to increase liquidity
Company issues new shares for cash
questions.explanation: A stock split divides shares into smaller units to make them more affordable and increase liquidity.

questions.text: The process of valuing a mutual fund’s portfolio at current market prices on a regular basis is called:
questions.explanation: Mutual fund portfolios are marked to market so that NAV reflects current market prices of underlying securities.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes a conflict of interest?
options: Advisor’s personal or financial interest clashing with duty to client
questions.explanation: A conflict of interest arises when the advisor’s personal or financial interests may compromise objective advice to the client.

questions.text: Benchmarking a portfolio is useful because it:
options: Removes the need for risk analysis
Provides a standard for performance comparison
questions.explanation: A benchmark represents a relevant market index or combination of indices used to evaluate portfolio performance.

questions.text: Book value per share is defined as:
options: Net worth ÷ number of equity shares
questions.explanation: Book value per share = (Shareholders’ equity ÷ number of equity shares).

questions.text: Credit counselling agencies help borrowers by:
options: Advising on debt management and repayment plans
questions.explanation: They guide borrowers on budgeting, negotiations and repayment discipline.

questions.text: Reducing interest rate but extending tenure on loan will generally:
options: Increase EMI and reduce total interest
Reduce EMI but may increase total interest paid
Reduce both EMI and total interest
questions.explanation: Longer tenure means lower monthly payment but higher cumulative interest.

questions.text: AMFI primarily functions as:
options: A mutual fund industry self-regulatory organization (SRO)
questions.explanation: The Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI) is an SRO promoting investor awareness and ethical conduct among mutual funds.

questions.text: Insider trading is best described as:
options: Using unpublished price-sensitive information for personal gain
questions.explanation: Insider trading involves using unpublished price-sensitive information, violating fairness and regulations.

questions.text: Portfolio Managers must report performance:
options: Uniformly across disclosure documents, marketing materials, and client reports
questions.explanation: Performance must be disclosed uniformly across all communications, as per SEBI’s performance disclosure norms.

questions.text: The interest component of an EMI in the first few months is:
questions.explanation: Initially, outstanding principal is high; hence interest dominates early EMIs.

questions.text: If an investor wants predictable cash flows and capital protection over a short horizon, which is MOST appropriate?
options: High-yield corporate bonds with low rating
Short-term debt fund or bank deposit
questions.explanation: Short-term debt funds or bank deposits focus on capital preservation and relatively predictable returns over short periods.

questions.text: The primary regulator for mutual funds in India is:
options: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI)
questions.explanation: SEBI regulates mutual funds under the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996 and subsequent amendments.

questions.text: An unsecured loan is one that:
options: Has no underlying asset pledged to the lender
questions.explanation: Unsecured loans rely solely on borrower’s creditworthiness rather than collateral.

questions.text: A convertible bond is:
options: A bond that can be converted into a fixed deposit
A bond with an embedded option to convert into a specified number of equity shares
A bond whose coupon converts from fixed to floating
A bond that can be converted into a government security
questions.explanation: Convertible bonds combine a plain bond with an equity conversion option, allowing bondholders to convert into equity shares.

questions.text: Whose primary responsibility is it to safeguard the interests of investors in a mutual fund?
questions.explanation: Trustees are appointed to oversee the mutual fund and protect the interests of the unit holders.

questions.text: If two assets are perfectly positively correlated, diversification will:
options: Have no effect on portfolio risk
questions.explanation: Perfect positive correlation (correlation coefficient = +1) means both assets move identically, offering no diversification benefit.

questions.text: A 'risk-averse' investor will:
options: Always choose the highest return regardless of risk
Prefer investments with lower risk for a given return
Ignore the level of risk while investing
questions.explanation: Risk-averse investors prefer lower risk for a given return and demand a risk premium for taking additional risk.

questions.text: An individual earns ₹12 lakh p.a., saves ₹3 lakh, and pays ₹1.2 lakh EMIs. His savings-to-income ratio is:
In the investor life cycle, the 'accumulation phase' is characterized by:
options: High net worth and focus on capital preservation
Building assets with higher risk tolerance and long horizon
questions.explanation: In the accumulation phase, investors are early in their careers, taking higher risk to build wealth over a long horizon.

questions.text: A credit score primarily indicates:
questions.explanation: Credit score measures probability of default; higher score means lower risk.

questions.text: Under SEBI rules, portfolio managers cannot make investments in:
questions.explanation: SEBI prohibits PMS from investing in below-investment-grade securities to protect investors.

questions.text: Modern Portfolio Theory (MPT) was first introduced by:
questions.explanation: Harry Markowitz introduced Modern Portfolio Theory in his 1952 paper 'Portfolio Selection', which mathematically demonstrated the benefits of diversification.

questions.text: Which body is set up by the Government to monitor financial stability and development?
questions.explanation: The Financial Stability and Development Council (FSDC) looks at financial stability, sector development and inclusion.

questions.text: The first step in initiating an investment relationship with a client is:
questions.explanation: KYC compliance is the first step before any investment transaction; it verifies the client’s identity and address.

questions.text: Which of the following small saving instruments is specifically targeted at the girl child?
questions.explanation: The Sukanya Samriddhi Account is a long-term small savings scheme specifically designed for the benefit of the girl child.

questions.text: Which is an example of good debt?
options: Loan to buy depreciating asset on EMI
questions.explanation: Borrowing for education or business that enhances earning potential is considered good debt.

questions.text: Financial markets primarily facilitate:
options: Movement of funds from surplus units to deficit units
questions.explanation: Financial markets channel savings from lenders/investors to borrowers/businesses, enabling efficient allocation of resources.

questions.text: Coupon yield is defined as:
options: Annual coupon divided by market price
Annual coupon divided by face value
Face value divided by market price
Market price divided by annual coupon
questions.explanation: Coupon yield = coupon payment / face value; it is the nominal coupon rate printed on the bond.

questions.text: The secondary market provides:
options: Liquidity and continuous price discovery for existing securities
questions.explanation: The secondary market offers liquidity and price discovery by allowing investors to trade existing securities.

questions.text: Churning of client portfolios refers to:
options: Rebalancing as per agreed asset allocation
Excessive buying and selling primarily to earn higher fees or commissions
Investing in multiple funds for diversification
Switching from regular to direct plans
questions.explanation: Churning is unethical when trades are executed unnecessarily to generate more brokerage or fees, not to benefit clients.

questions.text: Which of the following is a behavioural challenge in personal financial planning?
options: Availability of too many investment products
Client’s tendency to follow recent market trends blindly
questions.explanation: Herd behaviour and chasing recent performance are behavioural biases that can derail financial plans.

questions.text: If discretionary spending rises sharply, the likely outcome is:
options: Reduced surplus and possible debt increase
questions.explanation: Overspending reduces savings and may require borrowing.

questions.text: Which of the following advertising claims is UNETHICAL?
options: ‘Mutual funds are subject to market risks. Read all scheme related documents carefully.’
‘Our model portfolio has beaten FD returns over 10 years; future returns may differ.’
‘This strategy aims to outperform Nifty over the long term, but is not guaranteed.’
questions.explanation: Guaranteeing high returns with ‘zero risk’ is misleading and unethical as market products carry risk.

questions.text: From an adviser’s perspective, suitability of equity for a client depends on:
options: Risk tolerance, time horizon and financial goals
questions.explanation: Suitability assessment considers risk appetite, time horizon and objectives, not merely income or administrative details.

questions.text: In India, derivatives trading is regulated by:
options: SEBI under the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act
questions.explanation: Derivatives trading on exchanges is governed by SEBI under the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956.

questions.text: Which of the following is MOST consistent with ethical record-keeping?
options: Maintaining accurate, complete, and timely records of all client interactions and transactions
questions.explanation: Accurate and complete records support accountability, audits, and fair dispute resolution.

questions.text: All mutual fund distributors must hold a valid registration with:
questions.explanation: Distributors must obtain AMFI Registration Number (ARN) after completing the NISM Mutual Fund Distributors certification.

questions.text: The sponsor or manager must have a continuing interest in an AIF of not less than:
options: 2.5% of corpus or ₹5 crore, whichever is lower
2.5% of corpus or ₹5 crore, whichever is higher
5% of corpus or ₹10 crore, whichever is lower
questions.explanation: The continuing interest must be at least 2.5% of corpus or ₹5 crore, whichever is higher, ensuring alignment with investor interests.

questions.text: Clearing corporations mainly handle:
options: Settlement and risk management for trades
questions.explanation: Clearing corporations ensure smooth settlement of trades and manage counterparty risk.

questions.text: The Capital Market Line (CML) plots:
options: Expected return against standard deviation for efficient portfolios
Expected return against beta for all securities
questions.explanation: The CML shows the relationship between expected return and total risk (standard deviation) for efficient portfolios including the risk-free asset.

questions.case_text: Sneha earns ₹90,000 per month, spends ₹55,000, and pays EMIs of ₹20,000. She has health insurance cover of ₹4 lakh. She wants to build an emergency fund equal to 6 months of expenses.

questions.text: Monthly surplus available:
Target emergency fund size:

Where should she park the emergency fund?

questions.case_text: Amit and Neha, both aged 30, earn ₹1,00,000 per month jointly. They wish to buy a house worth ₹60 lakh in 5 years and also start saving for retirement at 60. Their current savings are ₹5 lakh invested in bank FDs. They can save ₹25,000 per month. Inflation is 6% p.a.

questions.text: Which of the following is Amit and Neha’s short-term goal?
questions.explanation: Emergency fund (3–6 months expenses) is short-term.

questions.text: Buying the house in 5 years is best categorised as a:
questions.explanation: Goals 3–7 years away are medium-term.

questions.text: Retirement planning is a ______ goal.
questions.explanation: Retirement lies 30 years ahead — a long-term goal.

questions.text: Their total monthly saving rate is:
To beat inflation over long term, they should allocate more to:
questions.explanation: Equities have potential to outperform inflation over long horizons.

questions.case_text: Neha received ₹5 lakh bonus and is considering investing either lump sum in an equity fund or via SIP over 12 months. The fund’s long-term return expectation is 10% per annum, and markets are volatile.

questions.text: Bonus amount received:
Investment options under consideration:
Expected return:

questions.case_text: Manoj has a home loan of ₹40 lakh at 8.5% p.a. for 20 years. His EMI is ₹34,700. He also has a personal loan of ₹5 lakh at 12% for 3 years. Monthly income ₹1 lakh.

questions.text: Total EMI burden per month (approx.):
questions.explanation: Personal-loan EMI ≈ 17 k → total ≈ 52 k.

questions.text: DTI ratio is roughly:
questions.explanation: 52 k ÷ 1 lakh = 52%. High → risky.

questions.text: To reduce DTI, Manoj should first:
questions.explanation: Personal loan has high rate; clearing it cuts DTI fast.

questions.text: Which loan is secured?
questions.explanation: Home loan is secured by property.

questions.text: If interest falls to 7.5% p.a., EMI reduces by about:
questions.explanation: Roughly ₹1 k drop per lakh interest cut on long-term loan.

questions.case_text: Rohit plans to buy a sedan costing ₹14 lakh. His bank offers a 5-year vehicle loan at 9% interest. He can either take the loan or use his mutual fund investments currently earning 6.5% p.a.

questions.text: Car price considered:
Loan rate offered:
Investment earning rate:
If he takes a loan, opportunity cost is due to:
Financially efficient option is:

questions.case_text: Arun invests ₹10,000 every year for 5 years in a recurring deposit earning 7% p.a.

questions.text: This is an example of:
questions.explanation: Equal yearly deposits form an annuity.

questions.text: Future value after 5 years is approximately:
If deposits are made at beginning of each year, value will be:
questions.explanation: Annuity-due earns an extra period’s interest.

questions.text: If rate increases to 8%, corpus will:
questions.explanation: Higher rate ⇒ higher future value.

questions.text: If Arun skips one year’s deposit, final corpus will:
questions.explanation: Missing a payment reduces total contribution and compounding.

questions.case_text: Sneha earns ₹1,00,000 per month, spends ₹65,000 and pays ₹20,000 in EMIs. She wants to build an emergency fund covering 6 months of expenses.
